text:
maria: Heads up — after the 09:00 rollout I see p99 spikes for short-sequence requests (<=64 tokens). p50/p95 look fine but p99 jumped ~400ms for several minutes. KV hitrate drops at the same time.
devin: timeline? did this line up with scale events or kernel selector changes? :thinking:
maria: scale events. Autoscaler kicked at 09:02 -> new worker pods came up around 09:16. Spike from 09:03–09:18. Logs show lots of kernel_fallback events while new pods warmed.
sam: do you have numbers? roughs are fine.
maria: p99 baseline ~220ms, peak ~620ms between 09:05-09:12. kv_cache_hitrate{pool="microbatch"} fell 0.92 -> 0.53 during scale-up window. Also saw higher kernel_switch_count on the new pods.
anya: that KV drop smells like cold cache on new hosts + prober sampling bias. If prober chooses a different kernel on small samples we can end up on a slower path.
kyle: which kernel switch? tiny->fast-attn or to the conservative kernel?
maria: conservative fallback more often. The kernel selector probes 5 samples by default; new pods return a mix of short requests (fast kernel) and a few medium ones that biased it toward the conservative path.
devin: two levers: increase prober sample size or make kernel selector use a two-stage decision with hysteresis. Increasing samples reduces noise but slows decision and may delay optimal kernel during rush.
sam: also autoscaler scale-up lag matters. If new pods are added and immediately get real traffic before their kv cache warms, tail suffers. We should pre-probe KV state or route initial traffic to warmed pool.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout/2026-03-17-09:00 by devops - version: runtime-v2.4.1
maria: I pulled flamegraphs from the worst pod. Hot path is single-threaded kernel entry: long memcpy on kv miss + fallback kernel path selection. See attached snippet from perf: (summarized)

```
# top stacks
42% runtime/kernel_fallback
18% runtime/kv_populate
12% runtime/memcpy
8% runtime/kernel_dispatch
```

devin: what does prober log show? sample breakdown?
maria: prober.log shows sample_size=5, sample_types=[short, short, medium, medium, short] -> median latency pointed to medium sequences -> chose conservative kernel.
anya: I'd be wary of simply upping sample_size in prod. Instead: adaptive prober that increases sample_count until confidence threshold reached, and bias initial samples toward short-seq (our common case).
kyle: can we bias by injecting synthetic short inference during new pod warmup? like a tiny warmup token stream to populate KV and confirm fast kernel.
sam: I'd prefer using prober.seed=true where orchestrator sends a warmup probe to new pods; those probes are counted separately and don't affect real-user metrics.
devin: also consider changing kernel switchover threshold: require 2x measured delta and a minimum sample_count before switching. That reduces flip-flopping at scale-up.
maria: agree. Proposed immediate mitigations:
- increase prober.min_samples from 5 -> 12 for new pods
- add prober.seed warmup traffic on scale events (config flag)
- bump kernel_hysteresis to 1.4x
devin: sounds good. small experiment: roll changes to a canary pool and run a 30m burst replay to measure p95/p99 and KV hitrate.
perf-bot: alert: p99_latency_runtime_microbatch > 500ms for 5 minutes (seen at 09:06) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: I ran a quick PromQL for reference:
```
sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) by (pod)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
kv_cache_hitrate{pool="microbatch"}
```
anya: let's not forget batching heuristics — during scale-up our batch_size cap was lowered to prioritize latency which reduced batching density and increased per-token overhead. Maybe temporarily allow slightly larger microbatch cap for warmups so kernel has better signal.
kyle: ok but track cost. larger microbatches = better throughput but could hurt tail if we block too long. set a short dynamic ceiling: max_batch_ms=12 for warmup period.
sam: action items:
1) devin + anya: implement adaptive prober (min 12 samples for new pods, confidence threshold) — experiment in canary (deploy next hour)
2) kyle: implement prober.seed warmup traffic in autoscaler (opt-in flag) — QA tomorrow
3) maria: prepare burst-replay script and PromQL dashboard for the canary test
4) infra-bot: label affected rollout as incident/P3
devin: timeline: canary deploy in 1h, 30m burn, gather p50/p95/p99 + kv_hitrate. I'll own metrics.
maria: thanks — I'll paste the perf logs to the ticket. ping me if you need traces. :eyes:
infra-bot: incident created: IN-2026-03-17-001 - assigned eng-runtime
kyle: one more note — if prober.seed causes too much warmup traffic we can route it to a separate warmup queue to avoid throttling customer traffic.
maria: agreed. will mark that as constraint in the ticket.
devin: if experiment looks good, we'll roll kernel_hysteresis change cluster-wide next week.
maria: closing loop for now. thanks all.
